newsitem.title: INDIA: India central banker sees rupee correction ahead.
newsitem.headline: India central banker sees rupee correction ahead.

text.p: A correction in the value of the Indian rupee is likely if demand for dollars from oil companies reemerges, a senior central bank official said on Friday.

"A correction cannot be ruled out if oil demand rebounds and industrial acitvity and imports pick up," Deputy Governor Y.V. Reddy of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) told a meeting of forex dealers in the southern resort state of Goa.
Reddy said the state-run Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has been resorting to external commercial borrowings, presumably in view of the lower cost of overseas funds and the perceived stability of the rupee.
This had depressed dollar demand in the forex market, he added. But he saw the effect being reversed shortly.
"You will have exactly the opposite effect when IOC reduces borrowings and makes cash payments," he said.
"The RBI's role is one of preventing undue appreciation or sharp depreciation," Reddy added. "A correction if any has to be gradual."
